profiles.name: Ellie Brett
profiles.description: Ellie Melvin Brett was implicated in a series of arson incidents in metro Atlanta during 2020, including the burning of multiple United States Postal Service vehicles outside a post office. He ultimately pleaded guilty in federal court to a conspiracy charge connected to those fires and was sentenced to a five-year prison term followed by supervised release, with an order to pay restitution. The incidents drew attention because investigators treated them as politically motivated property attacks occurring amid a volatile election year and widespread unrest.
profiles.finding: Antiracist Action2023 newsletter explicitly lists portrait; extraction/quality pending. Skater, rodeo and wedding namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Kyree Lee Robertson
profiles.description: In May 2020, Kyree Robertson participated in the Grand Rapids (MI) Riot as part of the Black Lives Matter protests. Robertson was accused of rioting and breaking into an ophthalmology office to steal glasses. He was also accused of lying to a police officer, but that charge was later dropped. Robertson pleaded guilty to both charges and was sentenced to a minimum of 23 months in prison, by far the harshest sentence out of all the rioters arrested that day. He was released from Parnall Correctional Facility at the end of 2024.
profiles.finding: Grand Rapids school court record appears in results; no verified portrait in exact/shortened queries.

profiles.name: Andrew Augustyniak-Duncan
profiles.description:
On May 30, 2020 during ongoing protests after George Floyd's murder, Andrew Augustyniak-Duncan was part of a civil disorder in Pittsburgh, PA that obstructed and adversely affected the interstate commerce of nearby businesses. He is accused of throwing projectiles which struck and injured several police officers. Sentenced to 41 months federal prison followed by 3 years of supervised release.

Andrew Duncan-Augustyniak was prosecuted in Pennsylvania state court for arson and related charges arising from the George Floyd Uprising protests in Pittsburgh on May 30, 2020. He is serving a state prison sentence at SCI Rockview.
profiles.finding: Audacy/KDKA and WTAE warrant reports have explicitly named photo leads; verification pending.

profiles.name: Justin Keezer
profiles.description: Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) water protector charged with criminal trespass for the June 2021 Fire Light ceremonial camp opposing Enbridge's Line 3 tar sands pipeline. White Earth Tribal Court dismissed his case in 2022, holding that Anishinaabe people retain sovereign treaty rights including the right to hold ceremony and protect the water.
profiles.finding: ICT case release confirms water protector; LakelandPBS/SEEKJOY interview visual leads. White Earth sports team name requires linkage.

profiles.name: Nancy Beaulieu
profiles.description: Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) water protector and organizer charged with criminal trespass for the eight-day Fire Light ceremonial camp at the Mississippi River headwaters in June 2021, opposing Enbridge's Line 3 tar sands pipeline. White Earth Tribal Court dismissed her case in 2022, ruling the action was a lawful exercise of sovereign Indigenous treaty rights.
profiles.finding: MN Reformer author matches MN350 water protector. Original194x166 too small, rejected; MPR and MN350 fundraiser promising follow-up. Influencer and Maine author namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Todd Thompson
profiles.description: Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) water protector charged with criminal trespass for the June 2021 Fire Light ceremonial camp opposing Enbridge's Line 3 tar sands pipeline. His case was dismissed by White Earth Tribal Court in 2022 on Indigenous-sovereignty and treaty-rights grounds.
profiles.finding: ICT case confirms identity, NewsFromStates cannabis case explicitly links Line3 prosecution; portrait review pending. Actor/astrophysicist excluded.

profiles.name: Adion Bryn Mallett
profiles.description: Adion Mallett, 22, was charged with rioting and possession of a firearm in the commission of a felony after he allegedly used a rock to hit a police officer in the shoulder when an Oklahoma City protest turned violent. Mallett admitted throwing rocks at officers but said he did not intend to hit them. He was found with a loaded pistol on his person and told officers he had it for protection from looting. Sentenced to 60 months in Oklahoma state prison.
profiles.finding: LinkedIn and business review name match but no independent case linkage; no accepted image.

profiles.name: Al M. Talaga
profiles.description: Al M. Talaga, 32, of Auburn, WA was arrested and charged federally as a felon in possession of a firearm. On June 1, 2020 Seattle PD responded to reports of a break-in at the Sneaker City store on Pike Street; suspects fled. Police impounded a Dodge Magnum traced to Talaga and found two loaded handguns inside (a .40 Glock and a stolen .40 pistol from a 2019 Tacoma home invasion). Talaga was prohibited from possessing firearms due to a 2005 King County Second Degree Robbery conviction. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Exact and shortened Seattle queries no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Alejandro Avalos
profiles.description: Alejandro Avalos, 28, was charged with depredation against U.S. property after a May 30, 2020 demonstration in Las Vegas, NV decrying George Floyd's death. As the night progressed protesters faced off against officers; some vandalized buildings and threw bottles, fireworks, and rocks; others gathered at the federal building and threw items to gain entry. A federal security guard was threatened. Sentenced to 21 months federal prison plus 2 years supervised release and $71,335.72 restitution.
profiles.finding: Peruvian photographer, Argentine footballer, Mexican doctor and Chilean victim namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Alexander Steven Heil
profiles.description: On May 28, 2020 as part of ongoing protests sparked by George Floyd's murder, Alexander Steven Heil, 24, joined and engaged with others to accelerate a fire in the Wells Fargo Bank building in south Minneapolis. Per defense filings, Heil "went to the Lake Street area to be part of the protest, drank too much and in a senseless, impulsive act while clearly under the influence of alcohol, threw a traffic cone into the existing fire." Sentenced to 30 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: StarTribune has court action still, portrait quality unverified; therapist and sculptor namesakes not established.

profiles.name: Andrew Darnell Carlisle
profiles.description: Andrew Darnell Carlisle, 29, of Atlanta was arrested on two counts of felony criminal interference with government property and one count of misdemeanor rioting after state investigators accused him of vandalizing the Georgia Department of Public Safety headquarters during a racial justice protest in July 2020. He was among a group throwing stones and incendiary devices through windows and spray-painting graffiti. As of September 2023 he was also charged in the Stop Cop City RICO case with 61 others. Sentenced to 1 month in Georgia state prison.
profiles.finding: Third-party booking listing exact fullname; original police/court source needed.

profiles.name: Andrew Moore Stegner
profiles.description: Andrew Stegner, 19, of Lynchburg, VA was charged with throwing a projectile into an occupied building (felony) and rioting (misdemeanor) after his participation in a Lynchburg Black Lives Matter protest in May 2020. He was allegedly part of a group that threw rocks at a restaurant after it was accused of publishing a racist tweet. Acquitted of the felony but found guilty of misdemeanor rioting; sentenced to 6 months prison with a 5-month suspended sentence.
profiles.finding: Exact and shortened Lynchburg queries no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Andrew Salvarani Garcia-Smith
profiles.description: Andrew Salvarani Garcia-Smith, 32, was charged for the burning of the Market House in Fayetteville, NC on May 30, 2020. He was caught on video throwing a bottle of burning liquid into the Market House and the burning liquid spilled back onto him, setting his hair and clothes ablaze. Sentenced to 27 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: WITN named codefendant image lead; verify which face and usable original before use.

profiles.name: Anthony Richard Couse III
profiles.description: Anthony Richard Couse III, 51, of West Palm Beach, FL (homeless at time of arrest) was charged with two felonies and two misdemeanors following his participation in a West Palm Beach BLM protest on May 31, 2020. He allegedly challenged Deputy Police Chief Rick Morris to a fight and egged on demonstrators. Pled guilty to lesser charges of felony resisting arrest with violence and misdemeanor disorderly conduct; sentenced to 2 months Florida state prison plus 18 months probation.
profiles.finding: Skier Law case report matches PalmBeach defendant; school memorial namesake not linked.

profiles.name: Antonio Wooden
profiles.description: Antonio Wooden, 23, was charged in Indianapolis with unlawful possession of a firearm by a fugitive from justice and as an unlawful user of a controlled substance after he was seen firing an AR-15 style rifle towards officers during the protests/riots in downtown Indianapolis. Sentenced to 32 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: WRTV shooting report matches Indianapolis case; musician not linked; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Darrian Mitchell Nguyen
profiles.description: Darrian Mitchell Nguyen was an Anoka, Minnesota, defendant investigated after an informant reported that he possessed firearms, explosive devices, and methamphetamine and wanted to join the anti-government Three Percenter movement. During the investigation, Nguyen discussed an interest in a revolution or coup d’état and arranged to obtain a short-barreled rifle fitted with an auto sear. Federal agents arrested him on October 4, 2022 after he took possession of the weapon and four auto sears. A search recovered the machine gun, twenty-two additional firearms, and an unregistered short-barreled shotgun. Nguyen pleaded guilty to possessing methamphetamine with intent to distribute and unlawfully possessing a machine gun. On July 27, 2023, he was sentenced to 77 months in federal prison followed by ten years of supervised release.
profiles.finding: CBS Minnesota and sentencing case corroborate Anoka defendant; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Aron McKillips
profiles.description: Aron McKillips was a Sandusky, Ohio, participant in the anti-government Boogaloo movement and was also reported by federal investigators to be a member of the New Sons of Liberty militia. The FBI alleged that between September 2021 and July 2022 he made at least five online threats to harm or kill law-enforcement officers, including posting a photograph taken while aiming a rifle at a nearby officer. Investigators also documented his possession and distribution of devices capable of converting semiautomatic rifles into machine guns. McKillips was arrested on November 1, 2022 and remained detained. He pleaded guilty to interstate communication of threats and unlawful possession of a machine gun and received concurrent 41-month prison terms on August 29, 2024, followed by three years of supervised release.
profiles.finding: 13ABC explicitly names Aron McKillips and Lucas County Jail credit; matching Sandusky case.800x450 image visually inspected, recognizable face; original retained.

profiles.name: Quintez Brown
profiles.description: Quintez Brown was a Louisville journalist, community activist, and city-council candidate who fired six shots at mayoral candidate Craig Greenberg inside Greenberg’s campaign office on February 14, 2022. Greenberg and four staff members escaped physical injury, although one shot grazed Greenberg’s sweater. Brown was arrested shortly afterward and released on bond two days later. Federal authorities rearrested him in April 2022. In his federal guilty plea, Brown admitted that he acted because Greenberg was running for mayor. He pleaded guilty to interfering with a federally protected activity and discharging a firearm in relation to a crime of violence. On January 24, 2025, he was sentenced to seventeen years and six months in federal prison followed by five years of supervised release.
profiles.finding: Kentucky HeraldLeader/AP case coverage portrait leads; Mississippi QuintezR booking excluded.

profiles.name: Ayoub Tabri
profiles.description: Ayoub Tabri, 24, of Arlington, VA was charged for the arson of a Pennsylvania State Police SUV during civil unrest in Philadelphia on May 30, 2020. PSP placed two patrol SUVs at the on-ramp for I-676 to prevent protestors from accessing the highway; a group attacked the vehicles, shattering windows and stealing road flares, fire extinguishers, and "riot bags" of PSP-issued equipment. Tabri allegedly threw a lit road flare into K1-17, igniting a fire that engulfed the SUV. Tabri was wanted by the FBI Philadelphia Joint Terrorism Task Force prior to capture. Sentenced to 30 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Inquirer case match; SkateJawn images BY Ayoub not automatically OF him; identity/crop follow-up.

profiles.name: Bailey Marie Baldus
profiles.description: On the night of May 28, 2020 Bailey Marie Baldus, 19, was caught on surveillance camera with co-defendants Mckenzy Ann Degidio Dunn and Samuel Elliot Frey at a St. Paul, MN health and nutrition store during the unrest after George Floyd's death. Charges against Baldus were dropped after her defense attorney argued she was in the building but did not participate.
profiles.finding: Federal affidavit and StarTribune dismissal match; no accepted portrait.
